big: A client started an SIP two years ago, mostly when prices were high. The market is now 13% lower and her statement shows a loss. She asks, 'Isn't an SIP supposed to protect me?' It helps with habit and cost, not with losses.

lines: I thought an SIP means no loss. Why is mine red?
An SIP is a method, not a product. It spreads your entry and builds a habit. It cannot stop a fall or promise a profit over any fixed period.

h: Same instalment, more units in a fall
alt: Monthly instalments buying more units at lower prices
caps: The same amount goes in every month.
When the price falls, it buys more units.
When the price rises, it buys fewer units.
Cost is spread, but a loss is still possible.

title: SIP facts
stops: An SIP is a way of investing, not a product
An SIP guarantees profit over two years
SIP returns are measured with XIRR
An SIP prevents losses in a falling market
caps: Returns come from the fund it invests in.
No method can promise a profit.
Each instalment goes in on a different date.
It cannot stop a fall in prices.

q: A client's two-year SIP shows a loss after a 13% market fall. What should the RM explain?
opts: The SIP is broken and must stop
An SIP does not prevent losses
The fund house made an error
SIPs always recover in a year
why: A loss in a fall does not mean the SIP is faulty.
An SIP is a method and cannot stop a fall.
Prices fell, so there is no sign of any error.
No method can promise recovery in a set time.

q: What does rupee cost averaging do?
opts: Buys the same units every month
Picks the lowest price each year
Buys more units when prices are low
why: Units vary because the price varies.
It cannot remove losses in a fall.
It does not pick any single price.
The same sum buys more units at lower prices.

q: Which measure suits an SIP, since each instalment goes in on a different date?
why: XIRR accounts for the date of each cash flow.
A point-to-point return assumes one lump sum.
Launch return ignores when the client invested.
The NAV alone ignores what the client paid.

q: A client says, 'My SIP will surely beat a fixed deposit in three years.' What is the right reply?
opts: Yes, if she adds more each month
why: No such rule exists for SIPs over three years.
Adding more money does not assure a better result.
Market returns are not assured over any short period.
SIPs can beat deposits over some periods.

pts: An SIP is a method. Returns come from the fund.
It builds habit and spreads cost but cannot prevent losses.
